outcome: Neonatal birth trauma composite (brachial plexus injury, cephalohematoma, subgaleal or subdural hematoma)
Severe neonatal composite (NICU admission, 5-min Apgar score less than 7, umbilical artery pH less than 7.1, intraventricular hemorrhage, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, or neonatal convulsions)
Maternal composite outcome (postpartum hemorrhage, third- or fourth-degree perineal tears or need for postpartum blood products)
Failure rate leading to cesarean delivery
cohort: The study included 1564 patients who underwent vacuum-assisted deliveries at a single tertiary center between 2011 and 2022, with a 1:1 matched analysis comparing 60-mm versus 50-mm Malmstrom cups.
finding: The use of a 60-mm Malmstrom cup in vacuum-assisted deliveries was associated with fewer cup detachments and a reduced risk of neonatal birth trauma and perineal tears, without increasing overall maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: Within vacuum-assisted deliveries, using a larger 60-mm Malmstrom cup reduced neonatal birth trauma and perineal tears compared to a 50-mm cup.
